question: What three major sciences are combined in nursing informatics?
explanation: Nursing informatics brings together nursing practice principles with computer and information science to manage clinical data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is informatics knowledge important for a modern bedside nurse?

options.A: It eliminates all paperwork in the hospital ward
options.B: It helps bridge raw data and clinical decisions
options.C: It allows nurses to fix broken hospital computers
options.D: It replaces the need for direct patient assessment

explanation: Digital tools and informatics systems organize patient information so nurses can make informed clinical judgments. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h1)

question: What tool uses scanning technology to verify patient identity before giving medicine?
explanation: BCMA matches the patient's wristband barcode with the medication package barcode to prevent medication errors. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h2)

question: A nurse receives a pop-up warning on the computer screen about a drug allergy when entering an order. What system generated this alert?
explanation: Clinical Decision Support Systems evaluate patient data in real-time to alert staff about safety hazards like drug interactions or allergies. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h2)

question: Where does point-of-care charting primarily take place?

options.C: At the central hospital billing office
options.D: Inside the medical records archive room

explanation: Point-of-care charting happens directly where the patient is located, using mobile devices or bedside terminals to record care instantly. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h3)

question: How does electronic documentation improve workflow efficiency for ward nurses?

options.A: By reducing time spent searching for lost paper charts
options.B: By allowing doctors to write prescriptions without nurses
options.C: By removing the need to ever assess vital signs manually
options.D: By automating the discharge of stable patients completely

explanation: Digital records are instantly accessible from multiple terminals, eliminating delays caused by misplaced paper files. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main advantage of a shared electronic health record for the healthcare team?

options.A: It allows doctors to work completely without nursing input
options.B: It automatically orders laboratory tests without clinician review
options.C: All professionals view up-to-date patient data simultaneously
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment

explanation: A shared electronic record ensures doctors, nurses, and pharmacists access the exact same current clinical information at the same time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are secure messaging systems inside hospital software important for patient care?

options.A: They allow quick communication between nurses and doctors
options.B: They replace formal shift handover meetings entirely
options.C: They store personal social media accounts for staff
options.D: They let patients chat directly with hospital management

explanation: Integrated secure messaging lets clinical staff exchange urgent patient updates rapidly and securely across departments. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h4)

question: What does evidence-based nursing practice rely on for clinical decisions?

options.A: Personal habits developed over many years
options.D: Verbal instructions passed down by seniors

explanation: Evidence-based practice uses current, validated research evidence to guide safe and effective nursing care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h5)

question: How do electronic health records support nursing research in a hospital?

options.A: By paying nurses extra money to conduct clinical studies
options.B: By preventing patients from refusing research participation
options.C: By writing research papers automatically for the nurses
options.D: By aggregating data to show which interventions work best

explanation: Data stored in electronic systems can be analyzed in bulk to evaluate treatment outcomes and improve future nursing protocols. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which security measure helps prevent unauthorized viewing of electronic health records?

options.C: Printing all patient files on paper

explanation: Unique logins and role-based access levels ensure that only authorized personnel can view specific patient health records. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is data management critical for hospital regulatory compliance?

options.A: It generates accurate reports on infection and mortality rates
options.B: It allows the hospital to hide medical errors from the public
options.C: It prevents nurses from working extra night shifts
options.D: It ensures patients pay their hospital bills in advance

explanation: Accurate digital record-keeping allows hospitals to produce required statistical reports for health authorities and accreditation bodies. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h6)

question: What health service allows nurses to monitor chronic patients remotely?
explanation: Telehealth uses telecommunications technology to deliver nursing care and monitoring to patients at a distance. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is telehealth particularly beneficial for patients in remote or rural areas?

options.A: It removes all costs associated with buying prescribed drugs
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never need hospital admission
options.C: It completely replaces the need for physical doctors forever
options.D: It reduces the need to travel long distances for simple follow-ups

explanation: Remote monitoring and virtual consultations bridge geographical gaps, making healthcare accessible to individuals far from major hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T3#GNS113_U1_T3_h7)
